findings.title: Re-triggering reference checks wholesale-overwrites submitted fraud_signals (form_session wiped)
findings.evidence: create_eligible_slots (trigger.gleam:201-211) calls stamp_creation_fraud unconditionally after the tx — even when inserted==0 (ON CONFLICT no-op). get_application_reference_contacts.sql selects WHERE application_id=$1 with NO status filter (returns submitted/terminal rows too). stamp_creation_fraud_signals.sql does a wholesale UPDATE reference_call SET fraud_signals = $2::jsonb WHERE id=$1 (no status guard). creation_fraud_signals emits form_session: null. run_action_with_prechecks (trigger.gleam:913) gates handle_start only on ownership + vacancy-active (no row-state guard), and create_eligible_slots' inserts are idempotent (ON CONFLICT) — i.e. re-calling is a supported, expected operation. The docstring's 'the trigger is idempotent (fires ~once per application)' is false: handle_start (trigger.gleam:444 -> run_create_checks) re-fires it on demand.
findings.detail: A landlord clicking 'Start reference checks' (handle_start) — or the viewed trigger re-firing — on an application that already has SUBMITTED reference rows wholesale-overwrites those rows' fraud_signals with the creation-time object (form_session: null), silently destroying the submitted form_session signals (completion_seconds, ip_matches_applicant, device_fingerprint_match, focus_seconds_reported, referee_ip, referee_user_agent) and re-running paid Twilio lookups. rc3-7's entire purpose is computing+persisting these signals; this path silently destroys them for any re-triggered application. Same root cause will also clobber RC4.3's referee_contact_invalid stamp (jsonb_set) once wired. The fraud_signals RESULT block (the referee's answers) is untouched; only the signals sub-object regresses, and submission is terminal so it is not recomputed.
findings.recommended_fix: Make the stamp idempotent/guarded: either (a) skip the stamp pass entirely when inserted==0 (no new rows → nothing creation-time to add), or (b) filter get_application_reference_contacts / the UPDATE to rows whose fraud_signals IS NULL (or to non-terminal rows), so submitted rows keep their form_session. Prefer (a) — simplest, matches the 'fires once' intent.

findings.title: cross_application_reuse + opt_nonempty + parse_count (+ opt_to_str) duplicated verbatim across form_handler.gleam and trigger.gleam
findings.location: server/src/reference_checks/form_handler.gleam:1366,1386,1402 + server/src/reference_checks/trigger.gleam:317,338,346 (opt_to_str pre-existing at trigger.gleam:1067, newly added in form_handler)
findings.evidence: Identical fn bodies for cross_application_reuse, opt_nonempty, parse_count in both modules (only the uuid.Uuid alias differs). AGENTS.md: 'DRY: extract helpers when logic repeats 2+ places.'
findings.detail: Two copies of the same SQL-contact/reuse helpers will drift; a SQL-signature change forces synchronized edits across modules. 3-source agreement (blind + architecture + Perkins verification).
findings.recommended_fix: Extract cross_application_reuse + parse_count + opt_nonempty + opt_to_str into a shared module (e.g. reference_checks/contacts.gleam, or fold the pure ones into fraud.gleam) and import from both call sites.

findings.title: fraud.carry_line_type has no test — empty / valid / unparseable branches all uncovered (the submission line_type carry, D3)
findings.evidence: grep carry_line_type over server/test/ → 0 matches. The fn has 3 branches ('' -> Unknown; valid line_type -> mapped; parse-error/missing-key -> Unknown) exercised only in production via form_handler.gleam:1345.
findings.detail: All three branches untested. Degrades honestly to Unknown (AD-10) so not a fabrication risk, but a regression (e.g. carrying a stale value, or a panic) would go uncaught.
findings.recommended_fix: Unit-test carry_line_type: '' -> Unknown; '{"line_type":"mobile"}' -> Mobile; unparseable/missing-key -> Unknown.

findings.title: Phase 1 trigger wiring (stamp_creation_fraud) is never asserted post-trigger
findings.evidence: server/test/integration/reference_checks_trigger_integration_test.gleam calls trigger.run_create_checks (lines 223,244,262,293,308,326,341,356) but asserts only Created(count:)/audit_count — never the fraud_signals column. stamp_creation_fraud runs as a side effect of every trigger test but its column write is best-effort + unasserted.
findings.detail: The SQL contract is pinned directly (reference_checks_fraud_integration_test), and the pure builder is unit-tested, but the orchestrator glue (cross_application_reuse, opt_nonempty, parse_count, the line-type call, error logging) could silently regress with no failing test. AC2 'at row creation' is not pinned end-to-end.
findings.recommended_fix: Add one integration test: after trigger.run_create_checks, read a row's fraud_signals and assert line_type/geo_vs_claimed_property/contact_reused keys are present (AC2).

findings.title: device_fingerprint_match_strength emitted but absent from the AD-10 table that says 'exactly these keys'
findings.evidence: form_session_block emits a 5th form_session key: #("device_fingerprint_match_strength", json.string("weak")). Spec AD-10 table lists 4 form_session keys (+D5 referee_ip/referee_user_agent); closing line: 'The object stored ... is exactly these keys.' 2-source agreement (blind + acceptance).
findings.detail: AC1 demands 'exactly the table above'. The extra sibling-label key is a scope deviation from the spec's 'exactly these keys' contract. Harmless data, but it diverges.
findings.recommended_fix: Either drop device_fingerprint_match_strength and convey the 'weak' caveat via RC4 rendering (constant/copy), or amend the AD-10 table to explicitly include the sibling-label key.

findings.title: Spec-named fraud.with_referee_contact_invalid Gleam fn + unit test not delivered (SQL stamp substitutes)
findings.evidence: Spec OWNS #1 + AC5 + Phase 3 name fraud.with_referee_contact_invalid(json) -> json.Json + a unit test. grep with_referee_contact_invalid over server/src → 0 Gleam matches (only spec markdown). The SQL jsonb_set stamp + integration tests (preserve-keys, null-column) are delivered instead. 3-source agreement (blind + acceptance + tests).
findings.detail: No behavioral gap — the SQL stamp achieves the same outcome and is tested. But it diverges from the spec's named pure-fn API and the 'fraud.gleam owns signals' separation (the stamp mutates a fraud signal partly in SQL).
findings.recommended_fix: Either add pub fn with_referee_contact_invalid(json) -> json.Json to fraud.gleam + a unit test (matching the spec), or update the spec/AC to record the SQL-stamp as the chosen mechanism.

findings.evidence: webhooks.gleam:12-13 module doc: 'Idempotent (claim_webhook_event, NFR-RC5) and sticky ...'. webhooks_integration_test.gleam:133: '// Re-delivery with the SAME svix-id — idempotent (claim 0 rows).'. findings.title: Phase 2 submit only partially integration-covered — focus_seconds_reported end-to-end, richer form_session fields unit-only
findings.evidence: The exit-routes submit test runs the full router->save_submit->build_submission_fraud_signals->complete_reference_call path and pins focus_seconds_reported (line 667). completion_seconds, ip_matches_applicant, device_fingerprint_match, referee_ip/ua, the DB-reuse re-run, and the line_type carry are asserted only in the pure-builder unit suite.

findings.title: effective_contact comment claims corrected='' falls back to snapshot, but code returns None
findings.evidence: Doc: 'A corrected "" is treated as absent (falls back to the snapshot).' Code: case corrected { Some(c) -> opt_nonempty(c); None -> snapshot }. For corrected=Some(""), opt_nonempty("") returns None — the snapshot branch only fires when corrected is None, not Some("").
findings.detail: The documented fallback for corrected="" never fires (Some("") -> None, not snapshot). Likely low impact (corrected_email/phone are probably stored as NULL when absent, not ""), but the comment misrepresents the code. Note the SQL convention (COALESCE(NULLIF(corrected_email,''), contact_email)) DOES treat corrected='' as snapshot, so the Gleam helper diverges from the SQL convention.
findings.recommended_fix: Either implement the documented fallback (Some("") -> snapshot), or correct the comment to state corrected="" yields None. Align with the SQL NULLIF convention either way.

findings.title: stamp_creation_fraud_signals doc says 'non-optional String' but generated type is Json (SQL directive says TEXT)
findings.evidence: Hand-written doc: 'Squirrel types fraud_signals as non-optional String (the JSON text)'. Generated signature: arg_2: Json (with pog.text(json.to_string(arg_2))). SQL directive: '--- stamp_creation_fraud_signals(reference_call_id: UUID, fraud_signals: TEXT)'.
findings.detail: Three sources disagree about the parameter type. Cosmetic doc inaccuracy; the generated code is correct (passes Json, serialises to string, casts ::jsonb).
findings.recommended_fix: Correct the doc to read 'Json' and align the SQL directive to JSONB so a Squirrel regen keeps the Json type consistently.
